scenes.headline: collect()
scenes.subtitle: Pulling all rows back to the driver as Python objects.
scenes.narration: The collect action pulls every row of a DataFrame back to the driver as a list of Row objects.

scenes.headline: What collect does
items: Returns all rows to the driver as a Python list
Is an action that triggers the full computation
Lets you loop over results in ordinary Python
Can crash the driver if the data is large
scenes.narration: Collect returns all rows to the driver as a Python list of Row objects. It is an action that triggers the full computation and lets you loop over results in ordinary Python, but it can crash the driver on large data.

scenes.headline: Collecting a small result
scenes.code:
config_df = spark.read.json("/config.json")
rows = config_df.collect()
for r in rows:
    print(r["key"], r["value"])
scenes.narration: We read a tiny configuration file, then collect it so the rows live in driver memory as a normal list. We loop over each Row and print its key and value, which is safe here only because the dataset is small.

scenes.text: Only collect data you know is small — otherwise you risk an out-of-memory crash.
scenes.narration: Only ever collect data you are sure is small, because pulling a large distributed dataset into one machine causes out-of-memory crashes.
